Recently, the FSC announced that in order to prevent investors from excessive leverage, the Joint Signature Center will establish an interbank credit inquiry mechanism for banks and brokers, which is expected to be officially launched at the end of October. In the future, after obtaining the customer's consent, the bank can grasp the customer's financing situation at the brokerage firm side. The brokerage firm can also inquire about the customer's borrowing situation at the bank side, making up for the supervision gap of the "half each" of the banking and securities systems in the past. Housing expert Li Tongrong described the policy in eight words: "It's not too late to be alert." He also suggested that the FSC should have a "three-view" policy: observe the flow of funds, observe the overall leverage, and observe the concentration of leverage. At the same time, we should pay attention to funds such as floods, excessive leverage to operate the stock market, and not pay attention to the chaos of four loans or multiple loans.
